question: For each of our German customers, how many orders have they placed, and how much have they actually paid us (only counting captured payments)? Show full name, order count, and total paid rounded to 2 decimals, highest payer first.
sql: SELECT c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS customer_name, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN p.status = 'captured' THEN p.amount ELSE 0 END)::numeric,2) AS total_paid FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id LEFT JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id WHERE c.country = 'DE' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name ORDER BY total_paid DESC, c.customer_id

question: Ignoring cancelled and refunded orders, how many distinct customers have bought something from each product category? List category name and customer count, most popular category first.
sql: SELECT c.name, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS distinct_customers FROM categories c JOIN products p ON p.category_id = c.category_id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status NOT IN ('cancelled','refunded') GROUP BY c.category_id, c.name ORDER BY distinct_customers DESC, c.category_id

question: Who are our top 5 customers by total spend, counting only delivered or shipped orders and including both discount and shipping in the total? Show their full name and total spend rounded to 2 decimals, biggest spender first.
sql: WITH order_totals AS (SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, SUM(oi.quantity*oi.unit_price) * (1-COALESCE(o.discount_pct,0)/100) + o.shipping_cost AS order_total FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status IN ('delivered','shipped') GROUP BY o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.discount_pct, o.shipping_cost) SELECT c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS customer_name, ROUND(SUM(ot.order_total)::numeric,2) AS total_spend FROM customers c JOIN order_totals ot ON ot.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name ORDER BY total_spend DESC, c.customer_id LIMIT 5

question: For each sales rep, how many distinct customers have they sold to, counting only orders that reached paid, shipped, or delivered status? Show rep name and customer count, most first.

question: For each sales rep, report their total revenue from delivered orders — item subtotal after any discount, excluding shipping — rounded to 2 decimals. Only include reps with at least one delivered order, ordered by revenue descending.
sql:
WITH ot AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, o.sales_rep_id,
         SUM(oi.quantity*oi.unit_price)*(1-COALESCE(o.discount_pct,0)/100) AS total
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
  GROUP BY o.order_id, o.sales_rep_id, o.discount_pct
)
SELECT e.employee_id, e.full_name, ROUND(SUM(ot.total)::numeric,2) AS total_revenue
FROM ot
JOIN employees e ON e.employee_id = ot.sales_rep_id
GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.full_name
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC, e.employee_id
archetype: multi-table JOIN (three or more tables)

question: For every product category, show the total units sold and total revenue (quantity times the price charged at order time, no discount applied) from delivered orders only, rounded to 2 decimals. Order by revenue descending.
sql:
SELECT c.category_id, c.name,
       SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_sold,
       ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity*oi.unit_price)::numeric,2) AS revenue
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id
WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
GROUP BY c.category_id, c.name
ORDER BY revenue DESC, c.category_id

question: For customers who were referred by another customer, list the referrer's full name, the referred customer's full name, and the referred customer's total captured payment amount across all their orders, rounded to 2 decimals. Only include referred customers who have at least one captured payment, ordered by that total descending.
sql:
SELECT r.first_name || ' ' || r.last_name AS referrer_name,
       c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS referred_name,
       ROUND(SUM(p.amount)::numeric,2) AS total_captured
FROM customers c
JOIN customers r ON r.customer_id = c.referred_by
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id AND p.status = 'captured'
GROUP BY c.customer_id, r.customer_id, r.first_name, r.last_name, c.first_name, c.last_name
ORDER BY total_captured DESC, c.customer_id
archetype: multi-table JOIN (three or more tables)

question: For each sales rep, count the distinct customers they've sold to and report total revenue (item subtotal after discount, excluding shipping) across orders that are paid, shipped, or delivered — ignoring pending, cancelled and refunded orders and any self-service web orders. Round revenue to 2 decimals and order by revenue descending.
sql:
WITH ot AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, o.sales_rep_id, o.customer_id,
         SUM(oi.quantity*oi.unit_price)*(1-COALESCE(o.discount_pct,0)/100) AS total
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.status IN ('paid','shipped','delivered') AND o.sales_rep_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY o.order_id, o.sales_rep_id, o.customer_id, o.discount_pct
)
SELECT e.employee_id, e.full_name,
       COUNT(DISTINCT ot.customer_id) AS distinct_customers,
       ROUND(SUM(ot.total)::numeric,2) AS total_revenue
FROM ot
JOIN employees e ON e.employee_id = ot.sales_rep_id
GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.full_name
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC, e.employee_id
archetype: multi-table JOIN (three or more tables)
style: formal reporting request from a manager

question: Among delivered orders placed by customers who opted into marketing, report the average order total (item subtotal after discount, plus shipping) per shipping country, rounded to 2 decimals, ordered by average total descending.
sql:
WITH ot AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, o.shipping_country,
         SUM(oi.quantity*oi.unit_price)*(1-COALESCE(o.discount_pct,0)/100) + o.shipping_cost AS total
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
  WHERE o.status = 'delivered' AND c.marketing_opt_in = TRUE
  GROUP BY o.order_id, o.shipping_country, o.discount_pct, o.shipping_cost
)
SELECT shipping_country, ROUND(AVG(total)::numeric,2) AS avg_order_total
FROM ot
GROUP BY shipping_country
ORDER BY avg_order_total DESC, shipping_country
archetype: multi-table JOIN (three or more tables)

question: For each product category, compute the average review rating and the number of reviews received by products in that category, including only categories with at least 5 reviews. Round the average to 2 decimals and order by average rating descending.
sql:

FROM reviews r
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = r.product_id
JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id

HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5

question: For each customer who has referred at least one other customer, report how many customers they referred and the combined revenue (item subtotal after discount, plus shipping) from those referred customers' delivered orders, rounded to 2 decimals; count a referred customer with no delivered orders as contributing zero revenue. Order by combined revenue descending.
sql:
WITH ot AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id,
         SUM(oi.quantity*oi.unit_price)*(1-COALESCE(o.discount_pct,0)/100) + o.shipping_cost AS total
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
  GROUP BY o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.discount_pct, o.shipping_cost
)
SELECT r.customer_id AS referrer_id,
       r.first_name || ' ' || r.last_name AS referrer_name,
       COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS referred_count,
       ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(ot.total),0)::numeric,2) AS referred_revenue
FROM customers r
JOIN customers c ON c.referred_by = r.customer_id
LEFT JOIN ot ON ot.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY r.customer_id, r.first_name, r.last_name
ORDER BY referred_revenue DESC, r.customer_id
archetype: multi-table JOIN (three or more tables)
style: formal reporting request from a manager

sql: WITH rep_orders AS ( SELECT o.order_id, o.sales_rep_id, SUM(oi.quantity*oi.unit_price)*(1-COALESCE(o.discount_pct,0)/100) AS total FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id=o.order_id WHERE o.status IN ('delivered','shipped') AND o.sales_rep_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY o.order_id, o.sales_rep_id, o.discount_pct ) SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(*) AS order_count, ROUND(SUM(ro.total)::numeric,2) AS total_revenue FROM rep_orders ro JOIN employees e ON e.employee_id=ro.sales_rep_id GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.full_name HAVING COUNT(*) > 15 ORDER BY total_revenue DESC, e.employee_id

         SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) * (1 - COALESCE(o.discount_pct,0)/100) + o.shipping_cost AS total

question: What was our monthly revenue from delivered orders in Q4 2024 (October through December), including discounts and shipping in the total? Round each month's revenue to 2 decimals and list earliest month first.

WITH order_totals AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date)::date AS month,
         SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) * (1 - COALESCE(o.discount_pct, 0) / 100) + o.shipping_cost AS total
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id

  GROUP BY o.order_id, month, o.discount_pct, o.shipping_cost
)

question: For every Sales department employee who has a manager, show the employee's name, their manager's name, and the manager's department, ordered alphabetically by employee name.
sql:
SELECT e.full_name AS employee_name, m.full_name AS manager_name, m.department AS manager_department
FROM employees e
JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.employee_id
WHERE e.department = 'Sales'
ORDER BY e.full_name, e.employee_id
archetype: self-join / hierarchy (category parent, employee manager, customer referrer)
style: casual business user asking a quick question
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: For subcategories that carry at least 3 products, show the subcategory name, its parent category name, and the average list price of its products rounded to 2 decimals, most expensive average first.
sql:
SELECT sub.name AS subcategory_name, top.name AS parent_name, ROUND(AVG(p.unit_price)::numeric, 2) AS avg_unit_price
FROM categories sub
JOIN categories top ON sub.parent_id = top.category_id
JOIN products p ON p.category_id = sub.category_id
GROUP BY sub.category_id, sub.name, top.name
HAVING COUNT(p.product_id) >= 3
ORDER BY avg_unit_price DESC, sub.category_id
archetype: self-join / hierarchy (category parent, employee manager, customer referrer)
style: casual business user asking a quick question
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

FROM customers c
JOIN customers r ON c.referred_by = r.customer_id
WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM c.signup_date) = 2024

question: For each manager who oversees sales reps, what's the total revenue (after discount, including shipping) from delivered orders placed through their direct-report reps? Round to 2 decimals and order by revenue, highest first.
sql:
WITH order_totals AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, o.sales_rep_id, o.status,
         SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) * (1 - COALESCE(o.discount_pct, 0) / 100) + o.shipping_cost AS order_total
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  GROUP BY o.order_id, o.sales_rep_id, o.status, o.discount_pct, o.shipping_cost
)
SELECT m.full_name AS manager_name, ROUND(SUM(ot.order_total)::numeric, 2) AS total_revenue
FROM order_totals ot
JOIN employees rep ON rep.employee_id = ot.sales_rep_id
JOIN employees m ON rep.manager_id = m.employee_id
WHERE ot.status = 'delivered'
GROUP BY m.employee_id, m.full_name
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC, m.employee_id
archetype: self-join / hierarchy (category parent, employee manager, customer referrer)
style: casual business user asking a quick question
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: For each top-level category, which of its subcategories has the highest average product price? Show the top-level category name, that subcategory's name, and the average price rounded to 2 decimals.
sql:
WITH sub_avg AS (
  SELECT sub.category_id AS sub_id, sub.name AS sub_name, sub.parent_id AS top_id, AVG(p.unit_price) AS avg_price
  FROM categories sub
  JOIN products p ON p.category_id = sub.category_id
  WHERE sub.parent_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY sub.category_id, sub.name, sub.parent_id
)
SELECT DISTINCT ON (top.category_id) top.name AS top_category, sa.sub_name AS subcategory, ROUND(sa.avg_price::numeric, 2) AS avg_price
FROM sub_avg sa
JOIN categories top ON top.category_id = sa.top_id
ORDER BY top.category_id, sa.avg_price DESC, sa.sub_id
archetype: self-join / hierarchy (category parent, employee manager, customer referrer)
style: casual business user asking a quick question
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: Looking only at delivered orders, what share of total revenue (order total including discount and shipping) does each shipping country account for, as a percentage rounded to 2 decimals? Biggest share first.
sql:
WITH tot AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, o.shipping_country,
    SUM(oi.quantity*oi.unit_price)*(1-COALESCE(o.discount_pct,0)/100)+o.shipping_cost AS order_total
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
  GROUP BY o.order_id, o.shipping_country, o.discount_pct, o.shipping_cost
)
SELECT shipping_country,
  ROUND((SUM(order_total) / SUM(SUM(order_total)) OVER () * 100)::numeric,2) AS revenue_share_pct
FROM tot
GROUP BY shipping_country
ORDER BY revenue_share_pct DESC, shipping_country
archetype: derived metric (order total with discount and shipping, margin, average rating, share of total, days to ship)

    SUM(oi.quantity*oi.unit_price)*(1-COALESCE(o.discount_pct,0)/100)+o.shipping_cost AS order_total

question: For 2024 orders that were paid, shipped or delivered, what's the average discounted item subtotal (ignoring shipping) per calendar month, rounded to 2 decimals? Show months in chronological order.
sql:
SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date) AS month,
  ROUND(AVG(t.subtotal*(1-COALESCE(o.discount_pct,0)/100))::numeric,2) AS avg_discounted_subtotal
FROM orders o
JOIN (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity*unit_price) AS subtotal
  FROM order_items
  GROUP BY order_id
) t ON t.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.status IN ('paid','shipped','delivered')
  AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_date) = 2024
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month
archetype: derived metric (order total with discount and shipping, margin, average rating, share of total, days to ship)

question: Among delivered orders that shipped within 3 days of being placed, and excluding self-service web orders, which 3 sales reps brought in the most revenue? Use order totals that include discount and shipping cost, rounded to 2 decimals, highest first.
sql:
WITH order_totals AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, o.sales_rep_id, o.status, o.shipped_at, o.order_date,
    SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) * (1 - COALESCE(o.discount_pct, 0) / 100) + o.shipping_cost AS total
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  GROUP BY o.order_id, o.sales_rep_id, o.status, o.shipped_at, o.order_date
)
SELECT e.employee_id, e.full_name, ROUND(SUM(ot.total)::numeric, 2) AS total_revenue
FROM order_totals ot
JOIN employees e ON e.employee_id = ot.sales_rep_id
WHERE ot.status = 'delivered' AND ot.shipped_at IS NOT NULL AND ot.shipped_at - ot.order_date <= INTERVAL '3 days'
GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.full_name
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC, e.employee_id
LIMIT 3
archetype: top-N / ranking with ORDER BY and LIMIT
style: casual business user asking a quick question

question: Looking only at shipped or delivered orders, and requiring at least 2 such orders per customer, which 5 customers have the highest average order total (including discount and shipping)? Return customer id, first name, last name, and the average rounded to 2 decimals, highest first.
sql:
WITH order_totals AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id,
    SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) * (1 - COALESCE(o.discount_pct, 0) / 100) + o.shipping_cost AS total
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id

question: Which products in the Furniture category have a stock quantity below 50? List the product name and stock quantity, ordered by product id.
sql: SELECT p.name, p.stock_qty FROM products p JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.category_id WHERE c.name = 'Furniture' AND p.stock_qty < 50 ORDER BY p.product_id

question: Which customers who signed up in 2023 have placed at least one cancelled order? List their full name and customer id, ordered by customer id.
sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.customer_id, c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS full_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.signup_date >= '2023-01-01' AND c.signup_date < '2024-01-01' AND o.status = 'cancelled' ORDER BY c.customer_id

question: For orders with status 'shipped', what's the total captured payment amount collected, rounded to 2 decimals?
sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(p.amount)::numeric, 2) FROM orders o JOIN payments p ON o.order_id = p.order_id WHERE o.status = 'shipped' AND p.status = 'captured'

question: How many reviews for the Cast Iron Skillet have a rating of 3 or below?

question: For delivered orders shipped to the UK, can you show me the order id, the customer's full name, and how they paid (only count payments that actually went through)?
sql:
SELECT o.order_id, c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS customer_name, p.method
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.status = 'delivered' AND o.shipping_country = 'GB' AND p.status = 'captured'

question: Which shipped orders from our German customers were handled by someone on the Sales team? Show the rep's full name, the customer's full name, and the order id, ordered by order id.
sql:
SELECT e.full_name AS rep_name, c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS customer_name, o.order_id
FROM orders o
JOIN employees e ON e.employee_id = o.sales_rep_id
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE e.department = 'Sales' AND c.country = 'DE' AND o.status = 'shipped'
ORDER BY o.order_id

question: For orders still sitting as pending that are headed to the US, list the order id, the product name, and the quantity for each item, ordered by order id then product.
sql:
SELECT o.order_id, p.name AS product_name, oi.quantity
FROM orders o
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
WHERE o.status = 'pending' AND o.shipping_country = 'US'

author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: For successful bank transfer payments on orders going to France, give me the payment id, the amount, and the customer's email, ordered by payment id.
sql:
SELECT pay.payment_id, pay.amount, c.email
FROM payments pay
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = pay.order_id
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE pay.method = 'bank_transfer' AND pay.status = 'captured' AND o.shipping_country = 'FR'
ORDER BY pay.payment_id

author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: Tomás Alvarez handles some of our accounts — for his delivered orders, show me the order id, the customer's full name, and the order date, ordered by order id.
sql:
SELECT o.order_id, c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS customer_name, o.order_date
FROM orders o
JOIN employees e ON e.employee_id = o.sales_rep_id
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id

question: For our customers living in Sydney, list every item they've ordered: the order id, the product name, and the quantity, ordered by order id then product.
sql:
SELECT o.order_id, p.name AS product_name, oi.quantity
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
WHERE c.city = 'Sydney'

author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: For products in the Cookware category, what total profit (the price charged minus unit cost, multiplied by quantity) came from delivered orders only? Return the product name and total profit rounded to 2 decimals, ordered by profit descending then product id ascending.
sql:
WITH profit AS (
  SELECT p.product_id, p.name, SUM((oi.unit_price - p.unit_cost) * oi.quantity) AS total_profit
  FROM products p
  JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
  JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  WHERE p.category_id = (SELECT category_id FROM categories WHERE name = 'Cookware')
    AND o.status = 'delivered'
  GROUP BY p.product_id, p.name
)
SELECT name, ROUND(total_profit::numeric, 2) AS total_profit
FROM profit
ORDER BY total_profit DESC, product_id ASC
archetype: two-table JOIN with a filter or aggregate
style: formal reporting request from a manager
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: How many distinct customers have referred at least one other customer who signed up? Return one number.
sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT referred_by) AS referrer_count
FROM customers
WHERE referred_by IS NOT NULL
archetype: two-table JOIN with a filter or aggregate

author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: What is the total amount collected from successfully captured payments on orders shipped to Great Britain (GB), rounded to 2 decimals? Return one number.
sql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(pm.amount)::numeric, 2) AS total_captured
FROM orders o
JOIN payments pm ON pm.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.shipping_country = 'GB'
  AND pm.status = 'captured'
archetype: two-table JOIN with a filter or aggregate
style: formal reporting request from a manager
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: Grouping by the customer's country, which countries generated combined item-subtotal revenue (ignoring discount and shipping) above $5000 from delivered orders? Return the country and total revenue rounded to 2 decimals, ordered by total revenue descending then country ascending.
sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT c.country, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS subtotal
  FROM customers c
  JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
  GROUP BY c.country
)
SELECT country, ROUND(subtotal::numeric, 2) AS total_revenue
FROM rev
WHERE subtotal > 5000
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC, country ASC
archetype: two-table JOIN with a filter or aggregate
style: formal reporting request from a manager
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: Among products in the Camping category that have received at least one review, what is each product's average review rating? Return the product name and average rating rounded to 2 decimals, ordered by average rating descending then product id ascending.
sql:
SELECT p.name, ROUND(AVG(r.rating)::numeric, 2) AS avg_rating
FROM products p
JOIN reviews r ON r.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE p.category_id = (SELECT category_id FROM categories WHERE name = 'Camping')
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.name
ORDER BY avg_rating DESC, p.product_id ASC
archetype: two-table JOIN with a filter or aggregate
style: formal reporting request from a manager
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: Considering only orders with status 'delivered' or 'shipped', what is the total quantity of items ordered for products whose current list price is above $400? Return one number.
sql:
SELECT SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity
FROM order_items oi
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
WHERE p.unit_price > 400
  AND o.status IN ('delivered', 'shipped')
archetype: two-table JOIN with a filter or aggregate
style: formal reporting request from a manager
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: Among customers who signed up in 2023, which ones have an average review rating below 3? Return their full name and average rating rounded to 2 decimals, ordered by average rating ascending then customer id ascending.
sql:
SELECT c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS full_name,
       ROUND(AVG(r.rating)::numeric, 2) AS avg_rating
FROM customers c
JOIN reviews r ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE c.signup_date >= '2023-01-01' AND c.signup_date < '2024-01-01'
GROUP BY c.customer_id, full_name
HAVING AVG(r.rating) < 3
ORDER BY avg_rating ASC, c.customer_id ASC
archetype: two-table JOIN with a filter or aggregate
style: formal reporting request from a manager
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: For sales rep Tomás Alvarez, what is the total revenue, including discount and shipping, from orders with status 'delivered' or 'shipped', rounded to 2 decimals? Return one number.
sql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(item.subtotal * (1 - COALESCE(o.discount_pct, 0) / 100) + o.shipping_cost)::numeric, 2) AS total_revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN employees e ON e.employee_id = o.sales_rep_id
JOIN (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS subtotal
  FROM order_items
  GROUP BY order_id
) item ON item.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE e.full_name = 'Tomás Alvarez'
  AND o.status IN ('delivered', 'shipped')
archetype: two-table JOIN with a filter or aggregate
style: formal reporting request from a manager
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: For each Sales-department employee, show their own full name, their manager's full name, and how many orders they've handled that reached delivered status, ordered by employee id.
sql:
SELECT e.employee_id, e.full_name AS employee_name, m.full_name AS manager_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS delivered_orders
FROM employees e
JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.employee_id
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.sales_rep_id = e.employee_id AND o.status = 'delivered'
WHERE e.department = 'Sales'
GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.full_name, m.full_name
ORDER BY e.employee_id
archetype: multi-table JOIN (three or more tables)
style: formal reporting request from a manager
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: List the review id, customer's full name, product name, and product category for every review with a rating of 1, ordered by review id.
sql:
SELECT r.review_id, c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS customer_name, p.name AS product_name, cat.name AS category_name
FROM reviews r
JOIN customers c ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN products p ON r.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN categories cat ON p.category_id = cat.category_id
WHERE r.rating = 1
ORDER BY r.review_id
archetype: multi-table JOIN (three or more tables)
style: formal reporting request from a manager
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: List the order id, customer's full name, product name, and quantity ordered for every order that included a discontinued product, ordered by order id then product id.
sql:
SELECT o.order_id, c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS customer_name, p.name AS product_name, oi.quantity
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE p.discontinued = TRUE
ORDER BY o.order_id, p.product_id

author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: For each customer country, how many distinct products have been bought in delivered orders? Show country and distinct product count, highest count first.
sql:
SELECT c.country, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS distinct_products
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
GROUP BY c.country
ORDER BY distinct_products DESC, c.country
archetype: multi-table JOIN (three or more tables)

author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: For every product in the Camping category, show its name, current stock quantity, and how many times it appears in an order item on a still-pending order, ordered by product id.
sql:
SELECT p.product_id, p.name AS product_name, p.stock_qty,
  COUNT(oi.order_id) FILTER (WHERE o.status = 'pending') AS pending_order_items
FROM products p
JOIN categories cat ON p.category_id = cat.category_id
LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
LEFT JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE cat.name = 'Camping'
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.name, p.stock_qty
ORDER BY p.product_id
archetype: multi-table JOIN (three or more tables)
style: formal reporting request from a manager
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: For every shipped order placed by a German customer, list the order id, customer's full name, and the total number of items (summed quantity) in that order, ordered by order id.
sql:
SELECT o.order_id, c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS customer_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_items
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE c.country = 'DE' AND o.status = 'shipped'
GROUP BY o.order_id, customer_name
ORDER BY o.order_id
archetype: multi-table JOIN (three or more tables)

author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: For every order handled by sales rep Priya Natarajan, list the order id, the customer's full name, the payment id, and the payment status for each of that order's payment records, ordered by order id then payment id.
sql:
SELECT o.order_id, c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS customer_name, pay.payment_id, pay.status AS payment_status
FROM employees e
JOIN orders o ON o.sales_rep_id = e.employee_id
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN payments pay ON pay.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE e.full_name = 'Priya Natarajan'
ORDER BY o.order_id, pay.payment_id
archetype: multi-table JOIN (three or more tables)
style: formal reporting request from a manager
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: 2024 signups who have at least one delivered order but have never left a single review — full name and their delivered-order count, highest count first, tie-broken by customer id.
sql: SELECT c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS delivered_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o.status = 'delivered' WHERE c.signup_date >= '2024-01-01' AND c.signup_date < '2025-01-01' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM reviews r WHERE r.customer_id = c.customer_id) GROUP BY c.customer_id, full_name ORDER BY delivered_count DESC, c.customer_id
archetype: multi-table JOIN (three or more tables)
style: terse power-user shorthand
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: For each manager, total revenue (item subtotal after discount, no shipping) from delivered orders handled by the sales reps who report directly to them. Round to 2 decimals, only managers with at least one such order, revenue descending.
sql: SELECT m.full_name AS manager_name, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - COALESCE(o.discount_pct, 0) / 100))::numeric, 2) AS revenue FROM employees m JOIN employees e ON e.manager_id = m.employee_id JOIN orders o ON o.sales_rep_id = e.employee_id AND o.status = 'delivered' JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY m.employee_id, m.full_name ORDER BY revenue DESC, m.employee_id
archetype: multi-table JOIN (three or more tables)
style: terse power-user shorthand
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: Discontinued items still sitting inside orders stuck at pending or paid (not yet shipped or delivered) — order id, product name, and customer full name, ordered by order id then product id.
sql: SELECT o.order_id, p.name AS product_name, c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS full_name FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE p.discontinued = TRUE AND o.status IN ('pending', 'paid') ORDER BY o.order_id, p.product_id
archetype: multi-table JOIN (three or more tables)
style: terse power-user shorthand
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: Per shipping country: total captured-payment amount from delivered orders placed by customers who did NOT opt into marketing. Rounded to 2 decimals, highest total first.
sql: SELECT o.shipping_country, ROUND(SUM(p.amount)::numeric, 2) AS total_paid FROM orders o JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id AND p.status = 'captured' JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' AND c.marketing_opt_in = FALSE GROUP BY o.shipping_country ORDER BY total_paid DESC, o.shipping_country
archetype: multi-table JOIN (three or more tables)
style: terse power-user shorthand
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: Orders that contain more than 3 distinct products — order id, customer full name, and the distinct product count, highest count first, tie-broken by order id.
sql: SELECT o.order_id, c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS product_count FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY o.order_id, full_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) > 3 ORDER BY product_count DESC, o.order_id
archetype: multi-table JOIN (three or more tables)
style: terse power-user shorthand
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: Per category: revenue (quantity times line price, ignoring discount and shipping) from US customers' orders that reached at least paid status — excluding pending, cancelled, and refunded orders. Category name and revenue rounded to 2 decimals, highest first, tie-broken by category id.
sql: SELECT cat.name AS category_name, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price)::numeric, 2) AS revenue FROM categories cat JOIN products p ON p.category_id = cat.category_id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.country = 'US' AND o.status IN ('paid', 'shipped', 'delivered') GROUP BY cat.category_id, cat.name ORDER BY revenue DESC, cat.category_id
archetype: multi-table JOIN (three or more tables)
style: terse power-user shorthand
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: Top 5 products by number of distinct GB or US reviewers who rated them 4 or 5 stars — product name, category name, and reviewer count, highest first, tie-broken by product id.
sql: SELECT p.name AS product_name, cat.name AS category_name, COUNT(DISTINCT r.customer_id) AS reviewer_count FROM products p JOIN categories cat ON cat.category_id = p.category_id JOIN reviews r ON r.product_id = p.product_id AND r.rating >= 4 JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id AND c.country IN ('GB', 'US') GROUP BY p.product_id, p.name, cat.name ORDER BY reviewer_count DESC, p.product_id LIMIT 5
archetype: multi-table JOIN (three or more tables)
style: terse power-user shorthand
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: Which customers have referred 2 or more other customers? List the referrer's full name and how many customers they referred, most referrals first.
sql: SELECT r.first_name || ' ' || r.last_name AS full_name, COUNT(*) AS referral_count FROM customers c JOIN customers r ON c.referred_by = r.customer_id GROUP BY r.customer_id, r.first_name, r.last_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 ORDER BY referral_count DESC, r.customer_id
archetype: GROUP BY breakdown with HAVING or a per-group aggregate

question: For each product, what is the total revenue (quantity times the price charged in order_items, across all orders regardless of status), rounded to 2 decimals? Only show products where this exceeds 3000, ordered by revenue descending.
sql: SELECT p.name, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price)::numeric, 2) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 3000 ORDER BY revenue DESC, p.product_id
archetype: GROUP BY breakdown with HAVING or a per-group aggregate
style: precise analyst specification that may name columns
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: For each manager, what is the average salary of the employees who report directly to them, rounded to 2 decimals? Only include managers with 2 or more direct reports, highest average first.
sql: SELECT m.full_name, ROUND(AVG(e.salary)::numeric, 2) AS avg_salary FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.employee_id GROUP BY m.employee_id, m.full_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 ORDER BY avg_salary DESC, m.employee_id
archetype: GROUP BY breakdown with HAVING or a per-group aggregate
style: precise analyst specification that may name columns
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: Group refunded orders by the calendar year of the order date and report how many refunded orders there were each year. Only show years with at least 3 refunded orders, ordered by year.
sql: SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date)::int AS yr, COUNT(*) AS refunded_count FROM orders WHERE status = 'refunded' GROUP BY yr HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 ORDER BY yr
archetype: GROUP BY breakdown with HAVING or a per-group aggregate
style: precise analyst specification that may name columns
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: For each product category, what is the average profit margin percentage ((unit_price - unit_cost) / unit_cost * 100) across its products, rounded to 2 decimals? Only include categories where this average exceeds 60, highest average first.
sql: SELECT c.name, ROUND(AVG((p.unit_price - p.unit_cost) / p.unit_cost * 100)::numeric, 2) AS avg_margin FROM products p JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.category_id GROUP BY c.category_id, c.name HAVING AVG((p.unit_price - p.unit_cost) / p.unit_cost * 100) > 60 ORDER BY avg_margin DESC, c.category_id
archetype: GROUP BY breakdown with HAVING or a per-group aggregate
style: precise analyst specification that may name columns
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: For each country, how many customers have opted in to marketing? Only show countries with at least 5 opted-in customers, most first.
sql: SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS opted_in_count FROM customers WHERE marketing_opt_in = true GROUP BY country HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5 ORDER BY opted_in_count DESC, country

style: precise analyst specification that may name columns
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: For each shipping country, count how many cancelled orders there were. Only show countries with 3 or more cancelled orders, most first.
sql: SELECT shipping_country, COUNT(*) AS cancelled_count FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY shipping_country HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 ORDER BY cancelled_count DESC, shipping_country
archetype: GROUP BY breakdown with HAVING or a per-group aggregate
style: precise analyst specification that may name columns
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: Which customers have written 2 or more reviews that include a title (excluding rating-only reviews)? List the customer's full name and the count of such reviews, most first.
sql: SELECT c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS full_name, COUNT(*) AS titled_review_count FROM reviews r JOIN customers c ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE r.title IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 ORDER BY titled_review_count DESC, c.customer_id
archetype: GROUP BY breakdown with HAVING or a per-group aggregate
style: precise analyst specification that may name columns
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: Which product categories contain more than 4 products? Show the category name and product count, highest count first.
sql: SELECT c.category_id, c.name, COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM products p JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.category_id GROUP BY c.category_id, c.name HAVING COUNT(*) > 4 ORDER BY product_count DESC, c.category_id
archetype: GROUP BY breakdown with HAVING or a per-group aggregate
style: formal reporting request from a manager
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: Which cities have 5 or more of our customers? List the city and the customer count, most customers first.
sql: SELECT city, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY city HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5 ORDER BY customer_count DESC, city

question: Which shipping countries have received more than 30 orders in total (any status)? Show the country and order count, most orders first.
sql: SELECT shipping_country, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY shipping_country HAVING COUNT(*) > 30 ORDER BY order_count DESC, shipping_country
archetype: GROUP BY breakdown with HAVING or a per-group aggregate
style: formal reporting request from a manager

question: For delivered orders only, what's the difference between the average order revenue (item subtotal after discount, plus shipping) of self-service web orders and orders that had a sales rep, rounded to 2 decimals? Self-service minus rep-assisted.
sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, o.sales_rep_id,
    (SUM(oi.quantity*oi.unit_price)*(1-COALESCE(o.discount_pct,0)/100)+o.shipping_cost) AS revenue
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
  GROUP BY o.order_id, o.sales_rep_id, o.discount_pct, o.shipping_cost
)
SELECT ROUND(
  (AVG(revenue) FILTER (WHERE sales_rep_id IS NULL) -
   AVG(revenue) FILTER (WHERE sales_rep_id IS NOT NULL))::numeric, 2) AS diff
FROM rev
archetype: NULL semantics (shipped_at, sales_rep_id, discount_pct, referred_by, review title)
style: casual business user asking a quick question
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: Looking only at orders that had a sales rep assigned and no discount applied, what's each rep's average order revenue (item subtotal plus shipping), rounded to 2 decimals? Give rep name and average, highest first, tie-break by employee id.
sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, o.sales_rep_id,
    (SUM(oi.quantity*oi.unit_price)+o.shipping_cost) AS revenue
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.sales_rep_id IS NOT NULL AND o.discount_pct IS NULL
  GROUP BY o.order_id, o.sales_rep_id, o.shipping_cost
)
SELECT e.full_name, ROUND(AVG(r.revenue)::numeric, 2) AS avg_revenue
FROM rev r
JOIN employees e ON e.employee_id = r.sales_rep_id
GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.full_name
ORDER BY avg_revenue DESC, e.employee_id
archetype: NULL semantics (shipped_at, sales_rep_id, discount_pct, referred_by, review title)

question: Which calendar quarter pulled in the most revenue from delivered orders (subtotal after discount plus shipping)? Give year, quarter number, and revenue rounded to 2 decimals, single row.
sql:
WITH order_totals AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, DATE_TRUNC('quarter', o.order_date) AS qtr,
    SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) * (1 - COALESCE(o.discount_pct, 0) / 100) + o.shipping_cost AS total
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
  GROUP BY o.order_id, o.discount_pct, o.shipping_cost, o.order_date
),
qtr_rev AS (
  SELECT qtr, SUM(total) AS revenue
  FROM order_totals
  GROUP BY qtr
)
SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM qtr)::int AS year, EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM qtr)::int AS quarter, ROUND(revenue::numeric, 2) AS revenue
FROM qtr_rev
ORDER BY revenue DESC, qtr
LIMIT 1
archetype: date and time (DATE_TRUNC, EXTRACT, month or year buckets, intervals, first/last event)
style: terse power-user shorthand

question: Ignoring self-service web orders, chain each sales rep's handled orders in date order and find the gap in days between consecutive ones. Which rep has the largest average gap? Give rep name and average gap in days, rounded to 2 decimals, single row.
sql:
WITH ordered AS (
  SELECT order_id, sales_rep_id, order_date,
    LAG(order_date) OVER (PARTITION BY sales_rep_id ORDER BY order_date, order_id) AS prev_date
  FROM orders
  WHERE sales_rep_id IS NOT NULL
),
gaps AS (
  SELECT sales_rep_id, AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (order_date - prev_date)) / 86400) AS avg_gap

  GROUP BY sales_rep_id
)

question: For orders currently sitting at 'paid' status, what's the average order total (including discount and shipping) broken down by customer country? Show country and average total rounded to 2 decimals, highest average first.
sql:
WITH item_totals AS (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity*unit_price) AS subtotal FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT c.country, ROUND(AVG(it.subtotal*(1-COALESCE(o.discount_pct,0)/100)+o.shipping_cost)::numeric,2) AS avg_total
FROM orders o
JOIN item_totals it ON it.order_id=o.order_id
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id
WHERE o.status='paid'
GROUP BY c.country
ORDER BY avg_total DESC, c.country

question: Find customers whose orders have shipped to more than one distinct shipping country. For each, show full name, the number of distinct shipping countries used, and their total captured-payment amount across all orders (treat customers with no captured payments as zero), rounded to 2 decimals. Order by distinct country count descending, then total captured descending, tie-broken by customer id.
sql:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS full_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.shipping_country) AS distinct_countries,
  ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN p.status = 'captured' THEN p.amount END), 0)::numeric, 2) AS total_captured
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
LEFT JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.shipping_country) > 1
ORDER BY distinct_countries DESC, total_captured DESC, c.customer_id

question: For orders placed by customers who signed up in 2024, and whose order status is anything except pending or cancelled, and which were handled by an in-house sales rep (not self-service web orders), compute total revenue per sales rep as item subtotal after discount plus shipping. Round to 2 decimals, ordered by revenue descending, tie-broken by employee id.
sql:
SELECT e.employee_id, e.full_name,
  ROUND(SUM(x.subtotal * (1 - COALESCE(o.discount_pct, 0) / 100) + o.shipping_cost)::numeric, 2) AS revenue
FROM employees e
JOIN orders o ON o.sales_rep_id = e.employee_id
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS subtotal
  FROM order_items
  GROUP BY order_id
) x ON x.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE c.signup_date >= '2024-01-01' AND c.signup_date < '2025-01-01'
  AND o.status NOT IN ('pending', 'cancelled')
GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.full_name
ORDER BY revenue DESC, e.employee_id
archetype: multi-table JOIN (three or more tables)
style: precise analyst specification that may name columns

question: For each product category, show the number of distinct customers who bought a product from it in a delivered order, and separately the number of distinct customers who left any review for a product in that category (regardless of purchase status). List category name, distinct buyer count, and distinct reviewer count, ordered by category id.
sql:
SELECT cat.category_id, cat.name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN o.status = 'delivered' THEN o.customer_id END) AS distinct_buyers,
  COUNT(DISTINCT r.customer_id) AS distinct_reviewers
FROM categories cat
JOIN products p ON p.category_id = cat.category_id
LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
LEFT JOIN reviews r ON r.product_id = p.product_id
GROUP BY cat.category_id, cat.name
ORDER BY cat.category_id

question: For each shipping country, find the single best-selling product by total quantity sold in delivered orders shipped there. Show shipping country, product name, and quantity sold, one row per country, ties on quantity broken by the lower product id, ordered alphabetically by country.
sql:
WITH sales AS (
  SELECT o.shipping_country AS country, oi.product_id, SUM(oi.quantity) AS qty
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
  GROUP BY o.shipping_country, oi.product_id
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT country, product_id, qty,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY qty DESC, product_id) AS rn
  FROM sales
)
SELECT r.country, p.name AS product_name, r.qty
FROM ranked r
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = r.product_id
WHERE r.rn = 1
ORDER BY r.country
archetype: multi-table JOIN (three or more tables)
style: precise analyst specification that may name columns

question: Which customers had a payment attempt fail before eventually getting a successful payment through on the same order? Show their full name, the order id, and how many failed attempts happened on that order, ordered by order id.
sql:
SELECT c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS full_name, o.order_id,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE p.status = 'failed') AS failed_attempts
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payments p2 WHERE p2.order_id = o.order_id AND p2.status = 'captured')
GROUP BY c.customer_id, o.order_id
HAVING COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE p.status = 'failed') > 0
ORDER BY o.order_id
archetype: multi-table JOIN (three or more tables)
style: casual business user asking a quick question
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: For delivered orders only, how much money did we effectively give away as discounts in each product category? Show category name and the total discount amount (item subtotal times the discount percent), rounded to 2 decimals, biggest giveaway first, ties broken by category id.
sql:
SELECT cat.name AS category_name,
       ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * COALESCE(o.discount_pct, 0) / 100)::numeric, 2) AS discount_amount
FROM categories cat
JOIN products p ON p.category_id = cat.category_id
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
GROUP BY cat.category_id, cat.name
ORDER BY discount_amount DESC, cat.category_id
archetype: multi-table JOIN (three or more tables)
style: casual business user asking a quick question
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: Find referred customers who've actually placed more orders than the person who referred them. Show the referred customer's name and order count, then the referrer's name and their order count, ordered by the referred customer's order count descending (ties by referred customer id).
sql:
WITH order_counts AS (
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT rc.first_name || ' ' || rc.last_name AS referred_name,
       COALESCE(oc1.cnt, 0) AS referred_order_count,
       rf.first_name || ' ' || rf.last_name AS referrer_name,
       COALESCE(oc2.cnt, 0) AS referrer_order_count
FROM customers rc
JOIN customers rf ON rc.referred_by = rf.customer_id
LEFT JOIN order_counts oc1 ON oc1.customer_id = rc.customer_id
LEFT JOIN order_counts oc2 ON oc2.customer_id = rf.customer_id
WHERE COALESCE(oc1.cnt, 0) > COALESCE(oc2.cnt, 0)
ORDER BY referred_order_count DESC, rc.customer_id
archetype: multi-table JOIN (three or more tables)
style: casual business user asking a quick question
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

question: For each sales rep, what's the average total (item subtotal after discount, plus shipping) of their delivered orders, rounded to 2 decimals? Only include reps with at least one delivered order, ordered by average total descending, tie-broken by employee id.
sql:
WITH order_totals AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, o.sales_rep_id,
         SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) * (1 - COALESCE(o.discount_pct, 0) / 100) + o.shipping_cost AS total
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
  GROUP BY o.order_id, o.sales_rep_id, o.discount_pct, o.shipping_cost
)
SELECT e.employee_id, e.full_name, ROUND(AVG(ot.total)::numeric, 2) AS avg_order_total
FROM order_totals ot
JOIN employees e ON e.employee_id = ot.sales_rep_id
GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.full_name
ORDER BY avg_order_total DESC, e.employee_id
archetype: multi-table JOIN (three or more tables)
style: casual business user asking a quick question
author: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id AND o.status = 'delivered'

question: Which products have an average review rating below 3? Show the product name, its category name, the number of reviews, and the average rating rounded to 2 decimals, ordered by average rating ascending, tie-broken by product id.
sql:

FROM products p
JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id
JOIN reviews r ON r.product_id = p.product_id

Order by revenue highest first, employee id as tiebreaker.
sql:
WITH order_totals AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, o.sales_rep_id,
    SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) * (1 - COALESCE(o.discount_pct, 0) / 100) + o.shipping_cost AS total
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
  GROUP BY o.order_id, o.sales_rep_id, o.discount_pct, o.shipping_cost
)
SELECT e.employee_id, e.full_name AS rep_name, m.full_name AS manager_name,
  ROUND(SUM(ot.total)::numeric, 2) AS revenue
FROM employees e
JOIN order_totals ot ON ot.sales_rep_id = e.employee_id
LEFT JOIN employees m ON m.employee_id = e.manager_id
WHERE e.department = 'Sales'
GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.full_name, m.full_name

question: For each employee who manages at least one direct report, add their own salary to the total salary of their direct reports, rounded to 2 decimals. Return the manager's employee id, name, and that combined salary figure, ordered by employee id.

  SELECT manager_id, SUM(salary) AS rep_salary
  FROM employees
  WHERE manager_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY manager_id
)
SELECT e.employee_id, e.full_name,
       ROUND((e.salary + COALESCE(r.rep_salary,0))::numeric, 2) AS total_salary
FROM employees e
JOIN reports r ON r.manager_id = e.employee_id
ORDER BY e.employee_id

question: For each subcategory, what percentage of its top-level category's total product count does it represent, rounded to 2 decimals? Return the top-level category name, the subcategory name, and that percentage, ordered by top-level category id then subcategory id.
sql:
WITH sub_counts AS (
  SELECT c.category_id, c.name, c.parent_id, COUNT(p.product_id) AS cnt
  FROM categories c
  LEFT JOIN products p ON p.category_id = c.category_id
  WHERE c.parent_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY c.category_id, c.name, c.parent_id
),
top_counts AS (
  SELECT parent_id, SUM(cnt) AS total_cnt FROM sub_counts GROUP BY parent_id
)
SELECT tc.name AS top_category, sc.name AS subcategory,
       ROUND(sc.cnt::numeric / tc2.total_cnt * 100, 2) AS pct_of_top
FROM sub_counts sc
JOIN top_counts tc2 ON tc2.parent_id = sc.parent_id
JOIN categories tc ON tc.category_id = sc.parent_id
ORDER BY sc.parent_id, sc.category_id
archetype: self-join / hierarchy (category parent, employee manager, customer referrer)

question: For each subcategory, what percentage is its average product list price of the overall average list price across all subcategories under the same top-level category, rounded to 2 decimals? Show the subcategory name, its parent category's name, and that percentage, ordered by subcategory id.
sql:
WITH sub_avg AS (
  SELECT c.category_id, c.parent_id, AVG(p.unit_price) AS sub_avg_price
  FROM categories c
  JOIN products p ON p.category_id = c.category_id
  GROUP BY c.category_id, c.parent_id
),
parent_avg AS (
  SELECT parent.category_id AS parent_id, AVG(p.unit_price) AS parent_avg_price
  FROM categories parent
  JOIN categories sub ON sub.parent_id = parent.category_id
  JOIN products p ON p.category_id = sub.category_id
  GROUP BY parent.category_id
)
SELECT sa.category_id, c.name AS subcategory_name, pc.name AS parent_name,
       ROUND((sa.sub_avg_price / pa.parent_avg_price * 100)::numeric, 2) AS pct_of_parent_avg
FROM sub_avg sa
JOIN parent_avg pa ON pa.parent_id = sa.parent_id
JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = sa.category_id
JOIN categories pc ON pc.category_id = sa.parent_id
ORDER BY sa.category_id
archetype: self-join / hierarchy (category parent, employee manager, customer referrer)

question: Which calendar month generated the highest revenue from delivered orders, counting the item subtotal after discount plus shipping cost? Return the month (truncated to month) and revenue rounded to 2 decimals, one row only.
sql: WITH order_totals AS ( SELECT o.order_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date) AS month, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) * (1 - COALESCE(o.discount_pct, 0) / 100) + o.shipping_cost AS total FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY o.order_id, o.order_date, o.discount_pct, o.shipping_cost ) SELECT month, ROUND(SUM(total)::numeric, 2) AS revenue FROM order_totals GROUP BY month ORDER BY revenue DESC, month ASC LIMIT 1

question: For products that have at least 3 reviews, what's the average gap in days between consecutive reviews (in chronological order)? Give me the product name and that average gap rounded to 2 decimals, longest average gap first, top 5, breaking ties by product id.
sql:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT product_id, created_at,
    LAG(created_at) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY created_at) AS prev_created
  FROM reviews
),
gaps AS (
  SELECT product_id, EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (created_at - prev_created)) / 86400 AS gap_days
  FROM ranked
  WHERE prev_created IS NOT NULL
),
agg AS (
  SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) + 1 AS review_count, AVG(gap_days) AS avg_gap
  FROM gaps
  GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT p.name, ROUND(a.avg_gap::numeric, 2) AS avg_gap_days
FROM agg a
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = a.product_id
WHERE a.review_count >= 3
ORDER BY avg_gap_days DESC, p.product_id
LIMIT 5

question: Comparing customers who were referred by another customer against those who weren't, what's the total spend of each group on delivered orders (order total including discount and shipping)? Return group label and total spend rounded to 2 decimals, highest first.

WITH order_totals AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id,
    SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) * (1 - COALESCE(o.discount_pct, 0) / 100) + o.shipping_cost AS total
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
  GROUP BY o.order_id, o.customer_id
)
SELECT CASE WHEN c.referred_by IS NULL THEN 'not referred' ELSE 'referred' END AS referral_status,
  ROUND(SUM(ot.total)::numeric, 2) AS total_spend
FROM order_totals ot
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = ot.customer_id
GROUP BY referral_status
ORDER BY total_spend DESC, referral_status

question: Looking only at delivered orders, and computing each order's total with discount and shipping included, which 3 calendar months brought in the most total revenue? Return the month (as a date) and the revenue rounded to 2 decimals, highest first.
sql:
WITH order_totals AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date) AS month,
    SUM(oi.quantity*oi.unit_price) * (1 - COALESCE(o.discount_pct,0)/100) + o.shipping_cost AS total
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
  GROUP BY o.order_id, o.order_date, o.discount_pct, o.shipping_cost
)
SELECT month, ROUND(SUM(total)::numeric,2) AS revenue
FROM order_totals
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY revenue DESC, month
LIMIT 3
archetype: top-N / ranking with ORDER BY and LIMIT
style: formal reporting request from a manager

question: Among products that have sold at least 10 units in delivered orders, which 5 generate the most revenue per unit sold (total revenue divided by total units, using the price actually charged)? Return the product name and revenue per unit rounded to 2 decimals, highest first.

  ROUND((SUM(oi.quantity*oi.unit_price)/SUM(oi.quantity))::numeric,2) AS revenue_per_unit
FROM products p
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id=p.product_id
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id=oi.order_id
WHERE o.status='delivered'
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.name
HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) >= 10
ORDER BY revenue_per_unit DESC, p.product_id
LIMIT 5

question: For delivered orders, how many different products do customers typically buy per order, broken down by shipping country? Round to 2 decimals, most products first, ties broken alphabetically by country.

WITH cnt AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, o.shipping_country, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS n
  FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
  GROUP BY o.order_id, o.shipping_country
)
SELECT shipping_country, ROUND(AVG(n)::numeric, 2) AS avg_products
FROM cnt
GROUP BY shipping_country
ORDER BY avg_products DESC, shipping_country

question: Looking only at orders paid by gift card that actually went through, what's the total revenue from those orders, including discounts and shipping? One number, rounded to 2 decimals.
sql:
WITH gc_orders AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT o.order_id, o.discount_pct, o.shipping_cost
  FROM orders o JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE p.method = 'gift_card' AND p.status = 'captured'
),
sub AS (
  SELECT g.order_id, g.discount_pct, g.shipping_cost, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS subtotal
  FROM gc_orders g JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = g.order_id
  GROUP BY g.order_id, g.discount_pct, g.shipping_cost
)
SELECT ROUND(SUM(subtotal * (1 - COALESCE(discount_pct, 0) / 100) + shipping_cost)::numeric, 2) AS total_revenue
FROM sub

question: Which product categories have an average list price higher than the store-wide average list price? Show category name and its average price, rounded to 2 decimals, pricier categories first.

question: For each customer, counting only successfully captured payments, what is their total amount paid? Only include customers whose total exceeds 500, rounded to 2 decimals, ordered by total paid descending.

question: Breaking orders down by the customer's own country (not the shipping destination), what percentage were self-service web orders with no sales rep assigned, rounded to 2 decimals? Only include countries with at least 10 orders, ordered by percentage descending, tie-break by country.

question: For products that are not discontinued, what is the average star rating per category counting only reviews that include actual title text (skip rating-only reviews), rounded to 2 decimals? Only include categories with at least 5 such titled reviews, ordered by average rating descending, tie-break by category name.
sql:
SELECT cat.name AS category_name, ROUND(AVG(r.rating)::numeric, 2) AS avg_rating
FROM reviews r
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = r.product_id
JOIN categories cat ON cat.category_id = p.category_id
WHERE p.discontinued = FALSE AND r.title IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY cat.name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
ORDER BY avg_rating DESC, cat.name
